items.title: A blow-up square that is a pushout with an injective leg produces a distinguished triangle
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when a commutative square has the property that the sheafification of the coproduct of two of its objects is the third and one leg is injective, the construction attached to the square yields a distinguished triangle of global section complexes, functorially in the complex (statement lines 6073-6089). The proof is a complete reduction to sheaves and a hand verification of exactness: a K-injective representative with injective terms reduces the assertion to a single injective sheaf (proof lines 6091-6095); exactness at the first arrow is read off from the pushout condition (proof lines 6101-6104); exactness at the last arrow uses injectivity and the description of sections as homomorphisms from a sheafified free sheaf (proof lines 6105-6110); and exactness in the middle is proved by factoring a map through the pushout and producing a unique amalgamation (proof lines 6113-6122). The non-formal content is the three exactness verifications. The claim is H2: a reduction followed by a written-out case analysis.
